name: deepwiki-codebase-wiki
description: Cross-platform codebase wiki generation with source-grounded documentation, deterministic Mermaid edge-label repair, regression tests, and separate authoring/render validation.

interface.longDescription: An additive ChatGPT runtime adapter for the original DeepWiki Skill. It preserves the six-phase workflow-runner contract, page-level workers when native concurrency is available, and truthful sequential fallback elsewhere. Version 2.0.7 synchronizes package documentation with the deterministic Mermaid flowchart edge-label lint/repair helper and keeps authoring-policy checks separate from actual parser/render outcomes.
interface.defaultPrompt: Use DeepWiki's original six-phase workflow and preserve the workflow-runner contract. Before writing, repairing, or validating any Mermaid diagram, read the packaged references/mermaid-authoring.md and references/mermaid-engine.md. These packaged references define the plugin's Mermaid authoring policy: use unquoted text inside pipe-delimited flowchart edge labels (A -->|Yes| B), while quoting node labels where appropriate. This is a deterministic style normalization rule, not a claim that Mermaid.js necessarily rejects a quoted label. Use tools/mermaid/mermaid_lint.py --check; when safe, use --repair --output to write a separate review copy, inspect the diff, and merge only intended generated/AUTOGEN changes back into the original page. Never overwrite the input or alter manual content outside AUTOGEN markers. Preserve middle-label syntax such as A -- "label" --> B and non-flowchart diagrams. Re-run static lint after repair. Static authoring lint is not Mermaid parsing. Report authoring_lint as passed/repaired/unresolved separately from renderer passed/failed/not_run. Only actual Mermaid.js parse plus SVG render or Mermaid CLI execution can produce renderer passed. If no renderer ran, renderer status is not_run. Run the packaged unittest regression suite when Python is available. On hosts with native concurrent Subagents, dispatch one independent workflow-runner per TOC page in parallel; otherwise use the honest sequential fallback.
